indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B1.4.3.1: Know that movement is caused by applied forces due to the release of stored energy
indicator.objective: Explain force as a pull or a push on an object

skills.description: Recognise pushing as a force that moves an object away from you
Recognise pulling as a force that moves an object towards you
Identify everyday activities that involve a push or a pull
Draw a picture showing a push or a pull in an everyday action

misconceptions: A push and a pull are the same thing.
Only pushing is a force; pulling is not.
You can only push or pull with your hands.
The wind does not push things.
Objects move on their own without any force.

questions.stem: When you push a door open, you are moving the door...
hints: You use your hands to move it forward.
You are not pulling it back.
questions.explanation: A push moves an object away from you.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think pushing moves an object towards them.

questions.stem: When you pull a rope towards you, you are...
hints: You are bringing it closer to you.
It is the opposite of pushing.
questions.explanation: Pulling moves an object towards you.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think bringing an object closer is pushing.

questions.stem: Which of these activities involves a pull?
options: Pulling a bucket from a well
hints: You bring the bucket up.
You use a rope.
questions.explanation: Pulling a bucket from a well involves a pull force.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think kicking is pulling.

questions.stem: Ama is pushing a wheelbarrow. Which direction is the force moving the wheelbarrow?
hints: She is moving it forward.
She is not pulling it back.
questions.explanation: Ama is pushing the wheelbarrow forward, away from her.
questions.misconception: Pupils may confuse the direction of a push.

questions.stem: Kwame is pulling a rope towards himself. What is he applying?
hints: He brings it closer.
He is not moving it away.
questions.explanation: Kwame is applying a pull force to bring the rope towards him.
questions.misconception: Pupils may confuse pulling with pushing.

questions.stem: Which of these is a push?
options: Opening a drawer by pulling the handle
hints: You use your foot.
You move the ball away from you.
questions.explanation: Kicking a football is a push force because you move the ball away from you.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think kicking is a pull.

questions.stem: When you push a swing, you move it...
hints: You stand behind it and move it forward.
You are not pulling it back.
questions.explanation: Pushing a swing moves it away from you.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think pushing a swing moves it towards them.

questions.stem: Adwoa is pulling a suitcase behind her. Which way is the suitcase moving?
hints: She drags it behind her.
She is bringing it along.
questions.explanation: Pulling a suitcase moves it towards her as she walks.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think pulling moves things away.

questions.stem: The wind blows and moves the leaves of a tree. Is this a push or a pull?
hints: The wind moves the leaves away.
The wind does not pull the leaves towards it.
questions.explanation: The wind pushes the leaves, moving them away.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think wind only pulls things.

questions.stem: If you move a table away from you, are you pushing or pulling it?
hints: You move it forward.
You are not bringing it towards you.
questions.explanation: Moving a table away from you is pushing.

questions.stem: If you bring a chair closer to you, are you pushing or pulling it?
hints: You bring it towards you.
It is the opposite of pushing.
questions.explanation: Bringing a chair closer to you is pulling.

questions.stem: Which of these is an example of a pull?
options: A man pulling a donkey cart
hints: The man is behind the cart.
He is bringing it along.
questions.explanation: A man pulling a donkey cart is an example of a pull force.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think throwing is a pull.

questions.stem: Kofi is trying to move a heavy box. He stands behind it and pushes. What happens to the box?
options: It stays in the same place
hints: Kofi is behind the box.
He moves it forward.
questions.explanation: When Kofi pushes the box from behind, it moves away from him.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think pushing pulls the box towards them.

questions.stem: Ama is pulling a bucket of water up from a well. She is applying a force...
options: That moves the bucket away from her
That moves the bucket towards her
That makes the bucket turn into a stone
hints: She is bringing the bucket up.
She wants the bucket to come to her.
questions.explanation: Pulling the bucket moves it towards Ama.
questions.misconception: Pupils may confuse the direction of pull.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT a push?
hints: Which action moves something towards you?
Pulling moves towards you.
questions.explanation: Pulling a rope is a pull force, not a push.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think all actions are pushes.

questions.stem: Why is a push considered a force?
options: Because it moves an object away from you
hints: Forces cause movement.
What happens to the object?
questions.explanation: A push is a force because it causes an object to move away from you.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think a force is just the feeling of being tired.

questions.stem: Which statement is TRUE about a pull?
options: It moves an object away from you
It moves an object towards you
It has no effect on the object
hints: Think about pulling a rope.
You bring it closer.
questions.explanation: A pull moves an object towards you.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think a pull pushes things away.

questions.stem: A boy is playing tug of war. He is pulling the rope towards his team. What force is he applying and in what direction is the rope moving?
options: A push, moving away from him
A pull, moving away from him
hints: He wants the rope to come to his side.
He is pulling.
questions.explanation: He is applying a pull force, and the rope is moving towards him.
questions.misconception: Pupils may mix up the direction of the force.

questions.stem: Draw a picture of a person pushing a wheelbarrow. Show the direction the wheelbarrow is moving.

criteria.description: Draws a person behind a wheelbarrow
Shows the wheelbarrow moving away from the person

hints: Where does the person stand?
Which way does the wheelbarrow move?
questions.explanation: This tests drawing a push force and its direction.

questions.stem: Draw a picture of a person pulling a bucket from a well.

criteria.description: Draws a person holding a rope and a bucket
Shows the bucket moving upwards towards the person

hints: Draw the rope going down to the bucket.
The bucket is coming up.
questions.explanation: This tests drawing a pull force and its direction.
